new_statements.rule_in_words: ǂHoan (ǂ'Amkoe) is described as a lexical tone language (four tone levels / register tonemes plus contours per Honken; three level tones L M H per Gerlach 2015 as summarised on Wikipedia). No opened source says anything about word stress or accent, and the table of contents of the dedicated phonology (Gerlach 2016, ch. 3 'Suprasegmentals') contains only tone and syllable structure, no stress section.
new_statements.domain_note: Statement concerns lexical tone on roots/stems in a comparative-historical paper; not a description of word-level prominence. The primary descriptions (Gerlach 2016; Collins & Gruber 2014; Honken 2013) could not be opened, so whether they explicitly deny word stress is unknown.
new_statements.identity_note: Glottolog hoaa1235 'Amkoe' (ISO huc) covers three varieties: Nǃaqriaxe [naqr1234] (Gerlach 2016's object), ǂHoan/ǂHȍã proper [huaa1249] (Collins & Gruber 2014; Honken 2013; Heine & Honken 2010, whose ǂHoan data come from Gruber's eastern-Kweneng fieldwork), and Sasi [sasi1238] (Collins 2024 dictionary). The quoted tonal statement refers to ǂHoan proper (Gruber's data). Older literature calls the whole language '(Eastern) ǂHoan'; not to be confused with 'Western ǂHuan', a Taa dialect.
